notes:
dashy 0.8.1

A small release about the first five minutes. A new install now starts in a
welcome, even when there are no notes yet.

A first launch explains itself. Before the folder picker opens, a short message
says what it is for: pick the folder your notes are in, or make a new empty one
with the picker's New folder button. If dashy was showing a folder that has
since been moved or renamed, it says so instead of opening a bare picker.

An empty folder gets a welcome, not a blank page. Opening dashy on a folder with
no notes used to show "No markdown found here yet" and nothing else. It now
shows a welcome with one button, Start with a starter note. That adds a
README.md and a TODO.md with three to-dos to try, then opens the folder's
dashboard, where ticking a box saves straight back into the file. It never
overwrites a file that is already there, and it does not need git.

Change folder. The small dashy window has a new Change folder button. Pick
another folder and dashy restarts on it.

Upgrading needs no manual step and there are no new schema migrations. If you
already use dashy on a folder with notes in it, nothing about your folder
changes.

Known and shipping unfixed, for the fifth release running: the Windows build
bundles keyring without its backends, so provider credentials fall back to
dashy's own file store rather than Credential Manager. Nothing is lost and the
fallback is the designed one.
